title: Earthlight
stanzas: A river bright with starry sin
Still in sight beneath the brine
Give your hand and take my fear
Cloak my hair in sunrise, sunrise
Fill my cup with morning dew
credit: Photo: Francesco Ungaro via Upsplash, with edits

title: Mother's Milk
stanzas: You take such comfort at my breast.
When I hold you close, we are safe
In a woolen world that's only ours,
Knitted just for us in my womb.
But I worry sometimes if you're drinking my sorrows.
If I'm passing it on like a virus.
Does it smell like my grandma's home
Does it taste like my father's brand of whiskey?
Does it bring you visions of everyone who never got to hold you?
Will you wake up one day, belly full, and forget how to dream?
All around me are women who break curses.
My mother and my cousin and my sister
All have crushed the head of their serpent,
Watched it spit its tail out its mouth.
But my curse lives inside me, buried in my skin
There is no serpent to crush.
There is no enemy at all.
Just this dark thing in me that I hope you cannot taste.
I hope it passes you like a shadow on the wall
Or a snake in the grass
But if it does find you
If you feel it squirming in places you cannot reach
Women in my family are great at breaking curses.
credit: Photo: Pornnaphat Suttiapiruk via Upsplash, with edits

title: Soft Hands
stanzas: Trying to catch moonlight in the palm of my hand
They don't pay you to love on company time
They told me my skin was too soft for the soil
The flesh on my hands has turned harder than stone
Dancing too slow in the hurricane's eye
credit: Photo: Alexander Mass via Upsplash, with edits
